question: According to Itamar Gilad, how should a company choose where to start when becoming more evidence-guided?
expected_points: Discuss internally to identify the company’s biggest problem.

sections.heading: Choose the starting point based on the biggest problem
sections.content: Discuss internally where the biggest problem is. If goals are unclear or teams are misaligned, start at the goals layer: clarify goals, establish a North Star and top business metric, build metrics trees, and give teams areas of responsibility. If debates and reversals dominate, work on evaluating ideas—using impact and confidence or another prioritization model that incorporates evidence; Gilad also recommends the confidence meter irrespective of the starting point. If the company builds too much without learning enough, start with the steps layer. If teams are disengaged, start with the tasks layer.

sections.heading: Adopt incrementally
sections.content: Do not attempt the whole transformation at once: Gilad warns that an overly large transformation can create fatigue and excessive process without visible results, leading people to give up. Treat the frameworks as a grab bag of tools—such as the confidence meter, ICE, or metrics trees—and begin with the one suited to the problem you identified.

answer.summary: Choose a starting point by discussing the company’s biggest problem, then adopt the relevant evidence-guided practices incrementally rather than attempting a full transformation at once. [S1]

sections.heading: Match the starting point to the problem
sections.content: Discuss internally where the biggest problem lies. If goals are unclear, teams are misaligned, or the company keeps pursuing the wrong things, start at the goals layer: clarify goals, establish a North Star and top business metric, build metrics trees, and assign teams areas of responsibility. If decisions get stuck in debates or keep changing, start with ideas: use impact and confidence, or another prioritization model that incorporates evidence. Gilad recommends the confidence meter regardless of the starting point. If the company builds too much without learning enough, start with the steps layer. If the team is disengaged, start with the tasks layer.

sections.heading: Adopt incrementally
sections.content: Don’t try to implement the whole system at once: an oversized transformation can cause fatigue, create process without visible results, and lead people to give up after a quarter. Select the practices that address the main problem and move closer to evidence-guided work progressively.
